text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe rules out dismissing national assembly and calling for early election or reshuffling government, says expects economic growth in 1997 to double from 1996. Economists polled by Les Echos expect two percent GDP growth next year.
-- British Airways asks European Commission to block sale of Air Liberte to AOM airline, which is up for sale by CDR structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets.
-- Publisher Balland interested in bidding for shipping company CGM, to be privatised soon.
-- Today is bidding deadline for companies wishing to buy controlling stake in CIC.
-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet to postpone plans of closing down Bank of France branch offices and restructuring.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Household consumption expected to post a 2.4 percent rise in 1996 in spite of high unemployment rate and flat buying power.

-- Eurotunnel to unveil debt-restructuring agreement with lender banks today, banks expected to take 49 percent of the Channel tunnel operator's capital in exchange for part of its 72-billion-franc debt.
L'AGEFI
-- Economists polled by the newspaper revise down three-month interest rates forecasts due to higher likelyhood of a European single currency, and budget austerity trends.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Pechiney to restructure, considers cutting some 2,700 jobs in Frnace.
-- National audit council's annual report criticises use of public funds by rail operator SNCF, builders of 34-billion-franc nuclear plant Superphenix, and in employment incentive schemes.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Stock exchanges worldwide buoyant in the wake of U.S. economy.
-- Gelatin manufacturers say their products are safe from BSE "mad cow" disease.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- British Airways seeks European Commission to block sale of Air Liberte to competitor AOM, itself up for sale under state-owned parent company Credit Lyonnais's restructuring plan.
